title: Property — historical Article 31 and Articles 31A–31C; Article 300A

content.overview: Article 31, the fundamental right to property, was omitted by the Forty-fourth Amendment. Article 19(1)(f) was omitted with it. Property is now a constitutional legal right under Article 300A: no person shall be deprived of property save by authority of law. Articles 31A, 31B and 31C remain. Article 31A saves certain laws of acquisition and estate modification from Articles 14 and 19. Article 31B protects Acts and regulations in the Ninth Schedule, subject to the case-law gate on judicial review. Article 31C saves laws giving effect to Article 39(b) or (c) from Articles 14 and 19, with the Forty-second Amendment extension and the declaration clause left on the case-law gate already noted in the DPSP subject.
content.study: Do not plead Article 31 as a living fundamental right. Use Article 300A for present deprivation. Open 31A, 31B or 31C only if that savings article is actually relied on. Do not reopen the DPSP lock.

sections.heading: Repeal of Art 31 as FR
sections.body: Forty-fourth Amendment omitted Article 31 from Part III. Use Art 300A for current deprivation-of-property claims.

learningObjectives: State that Article 31 and Article 19(1)(f) are omitted.
Identify Articles 31A, 31B and 31C as savings, with review flagged.
enhancement.definition: Property is no longer a Part III right. Article 300A requires authority of law. Articles 31A to 31C are savings, not a revived Article 31.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Deprivation of property needs the authority of law. A savings article is a shield for a qualifying law, not a cause of action for the owner.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Constitution of India, Article 300A; Articles 31A, 31B and 31C; Forty-fourth Amendment omission of Article 31.
essentialIngredients: Article 31 not pleaded as a fundamental right
Article 31A estate or acquisition law if that saving is used
Ninth Schedule item if Article 31B is used
Article 39(b) or (c) law if Article 31C is used
enhancement.detailedExplanation: The Forty-fourth Amendment removed the fundamental right to property and inserted Article 300A in Part XII. The owner's present plea is that the deprivation lacks authority of law. Article 300A is not enforced as Article 32 unless another Part III right is involved; the High Court writ remains available as a legal right. Article 31A saves specified acquisition and estate laws from Articles 14 and 19, with provisos on land under personal cultivation that must be read from the text before advice. Article 31B refers to the Ninth Schedule. Whether a Ninth Schedule law is immune from review is case-law and is not decided here. Article 31C is the Directive Principle saving already flagged in the locked DPSP topic.
examples: Land is taken without a statute. Article 300A is the plea, not Article 31.
A law claims Article 31A protection. The estate and acquisition conditions are checked from that article.
A Ninth Schedule Act is assumed untouchable. Article 31B is identified and review is left to the case-law gate.
enhancement.problemApplication: Date the deprivation. If it is current, use Article 300A. Use a savings article only as a defence to Articles 14 and 19, and flag review.
distinctions: Fundamental right vs constitutional legal right
Article 31A saving vs Article 300A cause of action
Article 31C vs a general Part IV override
enhancement.caseLawNotes: No new case citation or ratio was added. Names already in the published overview are not promoted to verified holdings.
enhancement.shortAnswerStructure: Article 31 is omitted. Property is Article 300A. Articles 31A to 31C are savings, with review flagged.

Ninth Schedule review is a case-law gate.
